item.title: Trump withdraws Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, as his nominee to lead ICE
item.description: The White House says it is withdrawing its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead ICE, ensuring that an agency at the forefront of President Trump's domestic agenda will remain without a Senate-confirmed leader for at least a while longer.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: The president made the remark to reporters amidst back-and-forth developments in federal court, including an allegation that a forklift repeatedly struck the center.

item.title: ICE agent appears in Minnesota court to face charges in the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant
item.description: Christian Castro, a federal immigration officer, made his first court appearance in Minnesota since he was booked Wednesday into a local jail. Castro faces multiple state and federal charges in connection with a shooting during the immigration surge in Minnesota.

item.title: Retired Olympic superstar Jessie Diggins wins her first-ever 100 mile trail race
item.description: This spring Jessie Diggins retired as one of America's most successful winter Olympic athletes at age 34. She's relaxing by entering 100-mile trail running races and navigating what comes next.

item.title: To prevent deaths in childbirth, Kenyan moms turn to an AI powered chatbot
item.description: Many questions come up during pregnancy. Is swelling normal? Are avocados safe to eat? For folks in Kenya who don't have a search engine at their fingertips, a chatbot is offering a lifeline.

item.title: A year ago, President Trump pledged to lower Medicaid drug prices. Has that happened?
item.description: The Trump administration's efforts to lower drug prices included promised changes to Medicaid. But it's still unclear which drugs will be affected. And each state has to opt in.

item.title: U.N.-backed experts cite possible U.S. war crimes in Iran, including a school attack
item.description: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N. say they have found "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab.
